- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing downside momentum.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope by 20–30%.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 10–15% downward bias to first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.4 to -0.4 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply “sentiment lag” correction: delay forecast shift by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
